"'''Love Will Lead You Back'''" is a song recorded by American singer [[Taylor Dayne]] for her second studio [[album]], ''[[Can't Fight Fate]]'' (1989). Written by [[Diane Warren]] and produced by [[Ric Wake]], the song was released on January 12, 1990, by [[Arista Records]] as the second [[Single (music)|single]] from the album.

"Love Will Lead You Back" reached number one on the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] in April 1990 and spent 15 weeks in the top 40, becoming Dayne's sole chart-topping hit in the US. It also reached number one on the ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' [[Adult Contemporary (chart)|Adult Contemporary]] chart and was certified [[RIAA certification|gold]] by the [[Recording Industry Association of America]] (RIAA). In addition to its US success, the song peaked at number two in Canada, number 11 in Australia, and number 28 in New Zealand.

"Love Will Lead You Back" is a song recorded by American singer Taylor Dayne for her second studio album, Can't Fight Fate (1989). Written by Diane Warren and produced by Ric Wake, the song was released on January 12, 1990, by Arista Records as the second single from the album.

"Love Will Lead You Back" reached number one on the US Billboard Hot 100 in April 1990 and spent 15 weeks in the top 40, becoming Dayne's sole chart-topping hit in the US. It also reached number one on the Billboard Adult Contemporary chart and was certified gold by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA). In addition to its US success, the song peaked at number two in Canada, number 11 in Australia, and number 28 in New Zealand.

sections.heading: Background
sections.wikitext: The song, written by American songwriter Diane Warren, is about a woman who is willing to set her lover free because she is confident that one day his love will lead him back to her; "''Sometimes it takes some time out on your own now / to find your way back home''". Warren has stated that she began writing the song while in a hotel in [[Russia]] and that she had [[Whitney Houston]] in mind to record it, but Arista Records president [[Clive Davis]] wanted to let Dayne record the song.
sections.text: The song, written by American songwriter Diane Warren, is about a woman who is willing to set her lover free because she is confident that one day his love will lead him back to her; "Sometimes it takes some time out on your own now / to find your way back home". Warren has stated that she began writing the song while in a hotel in Russia and that she had Whitney Houston in mind to record it, but Arista Records president Clive Davis wanted to let Dayne record the song.

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext: Matthew Hocter from Albumism stated that "Love Will Lead You Back" is "going on to be one of Dayne's most synonymous songs", noting "the phenomenal balladry" the singer delivered on the song.<ref>{{cite web|first= Matthew |last= Hocter |title= Taylor Dayne's 'Can't Fight Fate' Turns 30: Anniversary Retrospective |publisher= Albumism |date= October 5, 2019 |accessdate= November 17, 2020 |url= https://www.albumism.com/features/taylor-dayne-cant-fight-fate-turns-30-anniversary-retrospective}}</ref> Jose F. Promis from [[AllMusic]] described it as a "lush and dramatic" [[Sentimental ballad|ballad]].<ref>{{cite web|first= Jose F. |last= Promis |title= Taylor Dayne – ''Can't Fight Fate'' |publisher= [[AllMusic]] |date= |accessdate= November 4, 2020 |url= https://www.allmusic.com/album/cant-fight-fate-mw0000653904}}</ref> David Giles from ''[[Music Week]]'' wrote, "Something of a change in style for Taylor Dayne, this track from her [[Can't Fight Fate|current album]] is a big ballad in the [[Lionel Richie]] tradition and recently a US chart topper — so expect that success to be repeated over here."<ref>{{cite magazine|first= David |last= Giles |title= Singles |magazine= [[Music Week]] |date= July 21, 1990 |page= 19 |accessdate= October 30, 2020 |url= https://worldradiohistory.com/UK/Music-Week/1990/MW-1990-07-21.pdf}}</ref> A reviewer from ''[[People (magazine)|People Magazine]]'' noted that the singer can "dig for depth and rich tone on such ballads as [[Diane Warren|Warren]]'s "Love Will Lead You Back"."<ref>{{cite magazine | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201114110143/https://people.com/archive/picks-and-pans-review-cant-fight-fate-vol-33-no-1/ | archive-date=November 14, 2020 | url= https://people.com/archive/picks-and-pans-review-cant-fight-fate-vol-33-no-1/ |title= Picks and Pans Review: Can't Fight Fate |magazine= [[People (magazine)|People]] |date= January 8, 1990 |accessdate= November 13, 2020 | url-status=dead}}</ref>
sections.text: Matthew Hocter from Albumism stated that "Love Will Lead You Back" is "going on to be one of Dayne's most synonymous songs", noting "the phenomenal balladry" the singer delivered on the song. Jose F. Promis from AllMusic described it as a "lush and dramatic" ballad. David Giles from Music Week wrote, "Something of a change in style for Taylor Dayne, this track from her current album is a big ballad in the Lionel Richie tradition and recently a US chart topper — so expect that success to be repeated over here." A reviewer from People Magazine noted that the singer can "dig for depth and rich tone on such ballads as Warren's "Love Will Lead You Back"."

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext: The accompanying music video for "Love Will Lead You Back" was very simple. Directed by English director [[Nigel Dick]], it shows Dayne and her band in a [[Recording studio|studio]] performing the song. The music video was released both in [[Black and white|black-and-white]] and [[Photographic print toning#Sepia toning|sepia]] tones. In the music video, Dayne holds in her hand what seems to be the lyrics of the song, or possibly a letter from her lover.

sections.heading: Covers
sections.wikitext: The song was covered by [[Brazil]]ian singer [[Sandra de Sá]], [[Filipina]] singers [[Kyla (Filipino singer)|Kyla]], [[Nina Girado|Nina]] and Marika Sasaki, Filipino crooner Jun Polistico and Australian pop group [[Young Divas]]. Mexican showgirl [[Yuri (Mexican singer)|Yuri]] recorded a Spanish-language adaptation of the song as "Quién eres tú" on her studio album ''[[Soy Libre]]'' (1991).<ref>{{cite web |title=Soy Libre - Yuri {{!}} Songs, Reviews, Credits {{!}} AllMusic |website=[[AllMusic]] |url=https://www.allmusic.com/album/soy-libre-mw0000858403 |access-date=May 16, 2021 |language=en}}</ref> Yuri's version peaked at number eight on the ''Billboard'' [[Hot Latin Songs]] chart in the US.<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Yuri - Chart History: Hot Latin Songs |url=https://www.billboard.com/artist/yuri/chart-history/htl/ |magazine=Billboard |access-date=May 16, 2021}}</ref>
sections.text: The song was covered by Brazilian singer Sandra de Sá, Filipina singers Kyla, Nina and Marika Sasaki, Filipino crooner Jun Polistico and Australian pop group Young Divas. Mexican showgirl Yuri recorded a Spanish-language adaptation of the song as "Quién eres tú" on her studio album Soy Libre (1991). Yuri's version peaked at number eight on the Billboard Hot Latin Songs chart in the US.
